newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK STOCKS END UNCHANGED IN SLACK VOLUME.
newsitem.headline: GREEK STOCKS END UNCHANGED IN SLACK VOLUME.

text.p: Greek equities finished unchanged
after thin trading which fund managers attributed to the peak of
the summer vacation season.
"Macroeconomic indicators and corporate developments point
to a more vibrant stock market and higher prices," said a fund
manager who wished to stay anonymous.
But this necessitates higher trading volumes which will not
be the case as long as participants on both sides of the market
are on summer holidays, he added.
"Trading is low due to the holiday season but I do not
anticipate sentiment to improve considerably. No fresh positive
news is seen hitting the market in the near future," said a
floor trader.
"Interest rates are at a medium-term low and inflation has
neared its best levels for the year," the trader added.
The Athens benchmark index inched a mere 0.06 points higher
to 1,631.68 from Monday's 1,631.62, having oscillated within a
narrow seven-point band.
Turnover dropped to 7.5 billion drachmas on volume of 2.1
million shares.
There were block trades in Alpha Credit Bank ,
35,000 shares at 19,960 drachmas, Hellenic Bottling ,
10,000 shares at 11,100, and Aspis Pronia -- 46,500
shares at 2,380.
Decliners beat advancers 125 to 83 with 27 shares unchanged
on 235 traded.
OTE telecom Global Depository Shares (GDS) were
quoted on London's SEAQ International market at $11.0-$11.2. Two
GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike
price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at
1,128-1,158 drachmas.
The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread
warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at
10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,105-1,165 drachmas. The
warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying
stock edged up 5 drachmas to 6,500.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23
Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was
quoted at 676.18-719.35 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9
The ING Baring Financial Products American style call
warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at
$74.76-$77.57. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the
warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call
warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas
was quoted at 3,875-4,105 drachmas. The strike price is set at
10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a
basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $11.88 bid/no offer. The
strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9
The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma-
denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was
quoted at 244-277 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639
points and the warrants expire May 14 1998.
